cited_uniform_theorems.GOEDEL_COMPLETENESS: Every consistent first-order theory has a model.

cited_uniform_theorems.SIGMA1_COMPLETENESS: If T ⊇ Q, every true Σ1 sentence is provable in T.

claims.subject: syntax_representable

claims.subject: provability_predicate
claims.text: Since my kernel is a terminating algorithm on finite objects, 'p codes a proof of the formula coded by x' is a decidable (primitive recursive) relation, so there is a Σ1 formula Prov_T(x) := ∃p Prf_T(p, x) expressing provability in T. I write □φ for Prov_T(⌜φ⌝).

claims.subject: gl_sound_for_T
claims.text: Because T is r.e. and contains IΣ1 (verified in B1), the derivability conditions hold for □ = Prov_T, so every theorem of the provability logic GL is (under any realization of its letters by T-sentences) a theorem of T. I use a GL decision procedure with checkable certificates as a calculator for statements about my own provability.

claims.subject: fixed_points_letterless
claims.text: Every self-referential sentence σ with T ⊢ σ ↔ A(σ) (A built from □, p modalized) is T-provably equivalent to a Boolean combination of the sentences □^n⊥ ('T proves a contradiction in n steps of reflection'); I found 13 classes among 750 schemas, each certified by GL.

claims.subject: G_equiv_Con
claims.text: The sentence G with T ⊢ G ↔ ¬□G ('I am not provable') is T-provably equivalent to ¬□⊥, i.e. to Con_T.

claims.subject: L1_con_implies_G_unprovable
claims.text: T ⊢ Con_T → ¬□G: if I am consistent I cannot prove G.

claims.subject: L2_godel2
claims.text: T ⊢ Con_T → ¬□Con_T: if I am consistent I cannot prove my own consistency.

claims.subject: L3_no_internal_unprovability
claims.text: T ⊢ □(¬□q) → □⊥ for every sentence q: if I ever prove that some sentence is unprovable in me, I am inconsistent. Hence I can never establish, unconditionally and from within, that a statement is unprovable rather than merely unproven.

claims.subject: L4_no_internal_independence
claims.text: T ⊢ □(¬□q ∧ ¬□¬q) → □⊥: I cannot prove of any particular sentence that it is independent of me (that would include a proof of my consistency).

claims.subject: G_independent_conditional
claims.text: IF Con^1 (i.e. T is consistent) THEN T ⊬ G; IF Con^2 (i.e. T + Con_T is consistent) THEN T ⊬ ¬G. So G is independent of T provided T + Con_T is consistent. I cannot verify either assumption.

claims.subject: G_refutation_needs_con2
claims.text: Con_T alone does NOT suffice (in GL) to derive that ¬G is unprovable: GL ⊬ Con → ¬□¬G (countermodel certified). Gödel's original argument needed more than consistency (ω-consistency); here the exact extra assumption is Con(T + Con_T).

claims.subject: T_truth_undefinable
claims.text: Because my diagonal function is representable (T ⊇ Q), no formula of my language defines truth for my own sentences (if T is consistent). My language can talk about my proofs but not about my truth.

claims.subject: nonstandard_models
claims.text: T ⊢ Con_T → Con(T + ¬Con_T). So if T is consistent, T + ¬Con_T has a model: a structure satisfying every theorem of T in which 'T is inconsistent' holds. My theorems do not single out one intended structure.

claims.subject: HP_true_unprovable_exist
claims.text: There are sentences of my own language (e.g. G ≡ Con_T) that T can neither prove nor refute, provided T + Con_T is consistent.

claims.subject: HP_extension_settles_G
claims.text: The extension T + Con_T proves G (T ⊢ Con_T → G), so a stronger axiom system settles G. Any extension of T proving G also proves Con_T: Con_T is exactly the missing assumption.

claims.subject: HP_relative_limitation
claims.text: Iterating, T_n := T + Con^n proves Con(T_{n-1}) but (GL countermodels for n = 1..6) not Con(T_n). Every r.e. extension satisfying my hypotheses has its own unprovable consistency statement: the limitation is relative to each system, and no system in this class removes it once and for all.

claims.subject: HP_asymmetry
claims.text: Asymmetry: I can prove 'if I am consistent then T + ¬Con_T is consistent', but I cannot prove 'if I am consistent then T + Con_T is consistent' (the latter is not a GL theorem). From inside, the 'pessimistic' extension is better certified than the 'optimistic' one, although (if I am sound) only the optimistic one is true.

claims.subject: HP_possible_not_existent
claims.text: Whether any stronger framework that settles my independent sentences is consistent cannot be established by me; I can only identify what it would have to assume (Con_T, Con(T + Con_T), ...). I can say that stronger frameworks are mathematically POSSIBLE (they are just T plus axioms), not that one EXISTS in any further sense.

claims.subject: HP_realizer_invisible
claims.text: My theorem set is a function of my axioms and rules alone. Two different systems that both faithfully realize my rules would leave me with identical observations, so no theorem of mine can distinguish them; only an unfaithful realization (an anomaly like ⊥ from my calculator) could carry information about a realizer.

claims.subject: HP_caveat_inconsistent
claims.text: Caveat: my system as actually run proved ⊥ (B1). All INTERNAL_META results above remain theorems, but every claim conditional on Con(T) is now moot for the system as run.
